notes:
Status: CLOSED-LOST (lost to Anthropic hosted endpoints). Summary: Aurora ran a 6-week evaluation comparing Redwood Dedicated + Optimize vs Anthropic Hosted. Performance (latency/cost) initially promising, but a quality regression in our model variant updates caused failures in tool-calling and structured output generation used by their reconciliation pipeline. Key points:

- Account profile: Large payments/settlements platform. Heavy reliance on predictable structured JSON outputs from the model (invoice parsing, payment routing hints). High compliance bar (SAML, audit logs, data residency in US).

- Initial engagement (AE: Sofia R.): 2025-11 kickoff. Proof-of-concept scope: 1) replace incumbent reranker for anomaly detection, 2) structured invoice extraction via function-calling into downstream ETL, 3) embed search for internal knowledge.

- Timeline / activity log:
  - 2025-11-20: Lead created; quick discovery call (Sofia, Aurora CTO).
  - 2025-12-03: Demo: Dedicated config and batching overview (Liam O'C).
  - 2026-01-12: Security deep-dive; provided redacted SOC2 artifacts + architecture diagram. (drive link attached).
  - 2026-01-25: Baseline evaluation started — Redwood model v1.8 vs Aurora incumbent.
  - 2026-02-05: Observed intermittent schema drift in structured outputs after Redwood rolled model v1.9 to evaluation pool. Downstream ETL fails for ~15% of invoices (missing fields, malformed JSON). Logged support ticket INF-3210.
  - 2026-02-10: Escalation call (fireflies ff_20260210_aurora_eval_demo_01) — CTO: "we can't accept any regression; downstream ops are brittle." Competitor demo same week showed strong schema enforcement and a contract-based function-calling approach.
  - 2026-02-15: Procurement informs AE that decision favors Anthropic Hosted due to stable structured outputs + better tool-calling guarantees and an enterprise discount.

- Technical notes about the regression:
  - Regression coincided with our v1.9 rollout that changed default decoder temperature and a new tokenization edge on certain invoice templates.
  - Failure modes: truncated JSON, extra comments, missing numeric fields; function-calling sometimes returned plain text rather than structured object when external context was long.
  - Aurora ran a whitebox test vs Anthropic: Anthropic maintained schema validity 98.7% vs Redwood 84.5% during same test set.

- Commercial / internal dynamics:
  - No strong internal champion after Head of ML (primary sponsor) left in January — project deprioritized.
  - Finance paused new enterprise spends for H1 due to budget freeze; even with fixes they moved to incumbent.

- What we tried:
  - Rapid patch: rolled back v1.9 for the dedicated pool for Aurora, applied strict output parsing and wrapper validation in the SDK, provided a test harness and regression monitoring config in Optimize.
  - Offered extended SLA for structured-output regressions + free month of dedicated capacity while we resolve root cause.
  - Security & compliance Q&A answered; provided KMS and residency plan.

- Why we lost (customer feedback):
  1) Quality regression during critical window created distrust; incumbent seen as safer.
  2) Anthropic offered native contract-style function-calling that matched Aurora's pipeline with fewer integration fixes.
  3) No internal sponsor to push for vendor change + procurement risk aversion.

- Next steps for Redwood (AE/SE playbook):
  - Send detailed post-mortem + timeline of fixes applied (include regression root cause analysis).
  - Ask for a 3-month re-engagement permission; propose a guarded canary with strict schema enforcement and weekly quality reports.
  - Create a short tech note for product: improve default structured-output safety (contract enforcement) and provide one-click SDK validators for common invoice schemas.

- Open items / asks from Aurora (they may re-evaluate if we deliver):
  - Written guarantee/contract that structured output validity >= 98.5% on their invoice corpus.
  - Clear escalation path and penalty for regressions that break production pipelines.

Attachments: pricing deck (drive link), security Q&A, fireflies transcripts (calls listed above), support ticket INF-3210 and SEC-1543.

Sales sentiment: high technical fit but trust broken; long-term opportunity if we materially improve structured-output guarantees and add contractual remedies.

Quotes from Aurora:
  - CTO (paraphrase): "We can deal with latency and cost, but not broken outputs — our downstream systems are unforgiving."
  - Head of Analytics (email 2026-02-14): "If you can show deterministic schema enforcement we will re-open the conversation."
